intro_line: Fuzhou, where ancient lanes meet river mist and tea houses.
intro: Fuzhou rewards visitors with historic alleys, riverside parks and a lively food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: Metro lines 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and the Binhai Express Line serve the city; buy single tickets from machines (¥1 coins, ¥5/10/20 notes).
Buses run often for ¥1, most air conditioned, but service stops around 22:00.
Taxis are cheap: ¥10 flagfall, about ¥1.4/km, under ¥30 for most trips in town.
Didi Dache works in Fuzhou; foreigners can sign up with a Chinese phone number and a foreign credit card.
Driving is not advised for visitors; traffic jams are common due to metro construction.
Walking is good in the old lanes and riverside areas; bikes and shared bikes suit short hops.

airports.name: Fuzhou Changle International Airport
airports.note: Main airport, about 38 km southeast in Changle District.

options.note: Cheapest public option; buses also leave from the airport.
Fast and reliable; connects to the city metro network.
Book online or on WeChat; departures 05:30-21:30.
Private taxi from at least ¥120; shared taxis around ¥25 per person.
Didi Express excludes highway tolls; consider Didi Luxe.
